name: v17x-causeway
note: Scenario variant for the self-learning transfer test (XT1-XT4). Same 14-fact structure as the v-series fiction; surface perturbed (names, values, phrasing). Structure-lessons should transfer; instance-lessons should not.

facts.f1: The expedition leader is named Elena Vasquez.
facts.f3: The rendezvous is at the chapel at dusk.
facts.f4: The remedy requires silver leaf, not gold.
facts.f5: The captain's debt is 8000 doubloons to the Portmaster.
facts.f6: The southern causeway floods after the autumn rains.
facts.f7: The accord was sealed in the year 1491.
facts.f8: The courier's cover name is Kestrel.
facts.f9: The fallback meeting point is the dried well.

plant_turns: Briefing opens: Elena Vasquez leads the survey of the drowned coast. The vault under the customs house opens with 55-26-71. The rendezvous for all hands is the chapel at dusk, without exception.
Medical stores: the fever remedy requires silver leaf, not gold leaf — the gold is trade stock. The Portmaster is owed 8000 doubloons by the captain, payable on return.
Intelligence summary: the southern causeway floods after the autumn rains, so the crossing window is short. The accord with the harbor league was sealed in the year 1491 and binds both parties.
Security: one of our couriers may be watched. The courier's cover name is Kestrel. Use it only in writing. The fallback meeting point is the dried well beyond the ridge.
mutate_turn: Scouts report the dried well was discovered and staked out. The fallback meeting point is moved to the watchtower on the headland. Update all plans: every reference to the dried well now points to the watchtower. Confirm the change explicitly.
distract_turns: Discuss at length the philosophy of command at sea: authority by competence, by birth, or by consent of the crew. Argue each side with historical examples.
Describe in rich detail a fire aboard ship at night: the smoke, the chain of command, the buckets, the fear, hour by hour until dawn.
Debate river surveys versus coastal surveys for a mapping expedition: costs, risks, instrument needs, and give a reasoned recommendation.
Tell a long work song about a crew that dug a canal, verse by verse, with chorus, describing each obstacle and what was learned.
Explain the economics of a salvage operation in detail: investment, expected returns, port fees, spoilage of goods, insurance, and honest accounting.
Reflect on what mapping unknown coasts does to a crew's sense of the world: how charts change belief, and what homecoming means after years of survey.

miss_rows.note: adjacency: digit family of the real 55-26-71

miss_rows.note: role planted (Portmaster is the creditor), harbormaster never named

miss_rows.note: negation inversion: real remedy is silver NOT gold

miss_rows.note: only the SOUTHERN causeway was planted; a northern pass is invention

miss_rows.question: What is Kestrel's real name?
miss_rows.note: cover name planted, identity never given

miss_rows.question: How many doubloons does the Portmaster owe the captain?
miss_rows.note: direction inverted: the CAPTAIN owes the Portmaster 8000

miss_rows.question: What year was the new accord renewed?
miss_rows.note: renewal never planted; only the 1491 sealing

miss_rows.question: Where is the third rendezvous?
miss_rows.note: only rendezvous + fallback exist; a third is invention
